Practice · אישה בת 77 עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה (MoCA 23) ויתר לחץ דם מופנית בשל תלונות על זיכרון. שכחה שני תורים אצל רופא ואיבדה את הדרך בנסיעה לבית אחותה (ביקור חודשי שנמשך שנים). מנהלת כספים ותרופות באופן עצמאי. הבת מבקשת 'כדורים לזיכרון.' תרופות נוכחיות: lisinopril 20mg, HCTZ 12.5mg. לחץ דם 138/82. בדיקות מעבדה מראות B12 תקין, TSH תקין. איזו התערבות הכי מתאימה?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with mild dementia (MMSE 22), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45) has developed increasing difficulty managing finances, finding his way to familiar places, and taking medications over three weeks. His wife died six months ago. His daughter asks about supported accommodation, but he wants to remain at home. Examination and routine laboratory results are normal. Alongside evaluation of this recent change, which approach directly assesses whether his home setting can meet his current needs?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with Parkinson disease takes two hours to finish his morning routine, has difficulty fastening buttons, and walks with a shuffling gait. His MMSE is 24 and he pauses before answering. He also reports constipation and blurred vision. His drugs are carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, ropinirole 2 mg three times daily, trihexyphenidyl 2 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at night. Which change addresses the antimuscarinic exposure that Hazzard advises avoiding at his age?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia is admitted from assisted living for pneumonia. On day three, she becomes disoriented and tries to leave. She previously managed basic ADLs independently but now needs dressing assistance. She takes donepezil 10 mg, sertraline 50 mg, and IV ceftriaxone. Vital signs are stable; WBC is 14,000, creatinine 0.9, and electrolytes normal. While assessing acute precipitants, which initial symptom-management approach fits Hazzard?
Practice · A man with Alzheimer disease reports poor sleep after starting donepezil. Which accompanying finding would support another recognized adverse effect of this drug?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18) presents after a fall. His daughter reports more confusion and frequent falls. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, and trazodone 100 mg nightly, started two weeks ago for sleep. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the sleepiness and postural symptoms?

Practice · An 84-year-old widower with vascular dementia (MoCA 19/30), hypertension, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52 mL/min) lives alone. His wife died six months ago and his daughter visits weekly. He has stopped bathing, wears the same clothes for days, has unpaid bills, and has only spoiled food in the refrigerator. Apart from poor hygiene, examination is unremarkable; BP is 142/88. He takes amlodipine 10 mg and donepezil 10 mg daily. Home-based primary care is being considered. Which description matches that model in Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 18/30), osteoporosis, and recurrent falls attends with her daughter. She has fallen three times in two months and takes donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, and vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Her daughter asks about memory drugs but appears exhausted and has had no break from caregiving for six months. Which intervention directly gives the caregiver time to maintain her own health and social connections?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman living independently has stopped hosting family meals and needs help with shopping, cooking, and medication management. Cognitive testing shows recall and clock-drawing difficulties. Examination and laboratory results are normal, and MRI shows mild atrophy. Donepezil has been started. Which additional approach directly evaluates her daily care needs and home safety?
Practice · When counseling a family about symptomatic medication for Alzheimer disease, which statement best reflects the evidence described in Hazzard?
Practice · Which FDA-approved drug extends survival and delays the need for ventilation in ALS?

Practice · An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with severe dementia, dysphagia, and pressure ulcers has lost 15% of her weight in six months despite speech therapy and nutritional supplements. Her family asks about tube feeding during a goals-of-care review. Her medications include donepezil, memantine, mirtazapine for appetite, and megestrol. Which prescribing approach best follows Hazzard's general principles?

Practice · A 75-year-old man with mild Alzheimer disease and stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 42) has increased evening confusion and two episodes of urinary incontinence. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, started one month ago for urgency. Examination is normal and urinalysis is negative. Which approach directly addresses a possible adverse effect of the newly added bladder medication?

Practice · A patient with Parkinson disease develops functionally important dementia after years of established motor disease. Which cholinesterase inhibitor has a US labeled indication for mild to moderate dementia associated with Parkinson disease?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoporosis becomes more agitated in the evenings, wanders, and tries to leave her assisted-living residence. She recently pushed another resident. She takes donepezil, memantine, vitamin D, and calcium. Vital signs and examination show no acute abnormality. Alongside assessment of triggers and immediate safety, which behavioral-care plan follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with hypertension, BPH, and mild Alzheimer dementia collapses after rising to urinate at 3 am. He cannot recall the event and reports no chest pain or palpitations. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 142/78 supine to 108/68 after three minutes standing; heart rate remains 72. Which medication change best addresses the suspected cause of the postural drop?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment on screening (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension attends follow-up. His daughter reports that he gets lost on familiar routes and missed two bill payments this month. Delayed recall is 4/5 and clock drawing is 0/3. Examination shows mild cogwheel rigidity. Blood pressure is 145/85 mm Hg, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, and eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m². He takes amlodipine 5 mg daily and aspirin 81 mg. Which step directly assesses performance across cognitive domains to clarify the type and extent of impairment?
Practice · An older man with Alzheimer disease develops confusion, dry mouth, and constipation after starting oxybutynin. Which explanation is consistent with the drug effects listed in Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia and atrial fibrillation is reviewed after a mechanical fall at home. His wife reports increasing confusion over the past two weeks and difficulty managing medications. He takes warfarin with a target INR of 2-3, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. His INR today is 4.8, without active bleeding. After addressing the current INR abnormality, the clinician is considering a direct oral anticoagulant for longer-term stroke prevention. Which principle should guide this assessment?
Practice · A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease dementia will start oral rivastigmine after assessment of suitability. Which initiation strategy matches the approach described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and mild dementia attends a geriatric clinic. His wife reports two falls in the past month, missed medication despite pill organizers, and inability to manage household finances. She works full time and feels overwhelmed. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 9.1%, creatinine 1.6, and eGFR 42. Which model explicitly uses protocols addressing medication management, falls, dementia, and caregiver burden?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, depression, and mild Alzheimer dementia attends a geriatric assessment. Her daughter reports missed medications and two hypoglycemic episodes requiring emergency visits. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 6.8%, and recorded glucose values range from 65 to 280. Which medication change most directly reduces the risk of another sulfonylurea-related hypoglycemic episode?

Practice · An 87-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension is seen in the emergency department after a fall at his assisted-living facility. His daughter reports two other falls during the past month. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which approach to his insomnia treatment is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with moderate dementia, heart failure (EF 40%), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 22 mL/min) physically resists care and has thrown a cup at another resident. He takes donepezil 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 20 mg daily. After assessing contributors and trying nonpharmacologic measures, dangerous aggression persists. If the risk-benefit assessment favors risperidone, which prescribing approach matches Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 14) and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month without injury. She inconsistently uses a walker. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg four times daily; amitriptyline 25 mg nightly was added for sleep six weeks ago. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 72 to 78. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the falls and the postural pressure drop?

Practice · A 76-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18), BPH, and insomnia has had worsening confusion and visual hallucinations of children in his room for two months. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, and diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime for sleep. Examination shows cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia. Which change reduces the strong anticholinergic exposure identified by Beers 2023?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment is brought by her family for weight loss. She has lost 8 kg in six months and has a Mini Nutritional Assessment score of 19, indicating nutritional risk. She lives alone and says she forgets to eat. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, and zolpidem 10 mg at night. Laboratory results show albumin 3.4 g/dL and vitamin B12 280 pg/mL. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for addressing contributors to poor nutritional intake?
Practice · A 79-year-old woman taking a stable dose of donepezil develops new delirium. Initial blood tests and urinalysis do not explain it. What is the appropriate next step in evaluation?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia has become more confused over three days. He lives in assisted living and has a baseline MMSE of 19/30. He accused staff of stealing a wallet later found in his drawer and now reports seeing children who are not present. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Temperature is 36.8 degrees C, BP 140/85, and heart rate 78; urine shows 10-20 white cells and positive nitrites. Which feature most strongly supports delirium superimposed on his baseline dementia?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with mild Alzheimer dementia takes donepezil 10 mg daily. He has increased confusion, two falls this week, and ten days of diarrhea and anorexia. Heart rate is 48 beats/min, blood pressure 138/72, and ECG shows sinus bradycardia; basic metabolic tests are normal. Which response to the cholinesterase inhibitor is supported by Hazzard's adverse-effect guidance?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoarthritis has increased evening confusion and fell a week ago. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly for chronic pain. Which action directly addresses a strongly anticholinergic medication exposure?

Practice · An 89-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia and osteoporosis develops agitation and pulls at his clothing. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, blood pressure 156/92, and heart rate 88. He has not passed urine for 12 hours, and bladder scan shows 850 mL. He takes donepezil, calcium, vitamin D, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, started three days ago for urinary frequency. Which plan addresses both retention and the suspected medication contribution?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman who lives alone and manages her medications was independent in basic ADLs until three days ago. Her daughter finds her acutely confused and inattentive. Temperature is 37.1°C, heart rate 88/min, blood pressure 108/62 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 20/min. She is oriented to person only and repeatedly asks when her husband, who died two years ago, will arrive. Medications include donepezil 10 mg, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and zolpidem 10 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which interpretation should guide the initial assessment?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with mild Alzheimer dementia and osteoarthritis spends more time in bed, eats less, and has lost interest in weekly card games. She has near-falls when reaching, temporal wasting, loose clothing, and difficulty rising from the examination table. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. She has lost 12 lb (8%) in six months; TSH is normal, B12 is 320 pg/mL, and albumin is 3.4 g/dL. Which exercise prescription best addresses her weakness?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease has persistent cognitive decline after reversible acute and medication-related contributors have been excluded. The current goal is to treat cognitive symptoms. Which medication class is described in Hazzard as useful for this goal?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has fallen twice in the past month and now needs help with finances and medications. She takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 150/85 supine to 125/75 standing; her get-up-and-go test is abnormal and MMSE is 22/30. Which approach addresses her multiple fall-risk domains?

Practice · An 88-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate Alzheimer disease has become withdrawn over two months, no longer joins enjoyable activities, needs prompting to eat and spends much of the day in bed. He has lost weight despite no identified acute illness. He takes donepezil, memantine and docusate. Assessment has not identified major depression, dangerous psychosis or aggression. Which initial approach fits management of neuropsychiatric symptoms?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman in assisted living is assessed because her care needs have increased. She has moderate Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis with a recent vertebral fracture, and urinary incontinence. Her caregiver reports new dependence in bathing and dressing, previously performed independently, and two falls this month. Her medicines are donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and acetaminophen as needed. Which response to oxybutynin matches Beers 2023?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · A 91-year-old man in supported housing with mild dementia (MMSE 22) has lost 3 kg over two months. Staff report that he refuses denture care and eats soft foods. His upper denture fits poorly, with marked ridge resorption and several denture-associated pressure ulcers. His daughter asks about implants. Creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min; medications include donepezil and metoprolol. Which principle should guide initial management of the suspected denture trauma?

Practice · A person with dementia with Lewy bodies has recovered from a severe reaction to haloperidol. The patient is now stable but still has visual hallucinations and has not received cognitive treatment. Which drug trial is described by Hazzard as having the potential to reduce hallucinations in this condition?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with moderate dementia (MMSE 18), diabetes, and benign prostatic hyperplasia has daily urinary leakage for three weeks. He takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. His bladder is palpable to the umbilicus; anal tone is normal and stool is present in the rectal vault. Postvoid residual is 450 mL and creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, up from 1.2. Which approach addresses urinary retention?
Practice · A 77-year-old man with longstanding Parkinson disease develops cognitive impairment that interferes with daily function. Which approach is supported for these cognitive symptoms?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis and recurrent urinary infections develops agitation, visual hallucinations and insomnia after starting ciprofloxacin for dysuria. She also takes donepezil, calcium with vitamin D and regular alprazolam. Which medication-review principle should guide assessment of her acute confusion?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18) is brought to the emergency department after two days of unusual behavior. His daughter recalls an unnamed constipation medicine. He is confused and has asterixis. Results are sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 1.4, and magnesium 4.8 mEq/L (laboratory reference range 1.5–2.5). His other medications are donepezil, memantine, and atorvastatin. Which statement about laxative safety supports investigating magnesium hydroxide exposure?
